CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING AGENDA
  “We are a vibrant, livable, and inclusive community dedicated to quality services,
  safety, financial strength, sustainability, preservation, and progress
  with equal representation for our community.”

City Council Chamber  Tuesday
225 Second Street  February 22, 2022
Claremont, CA 91711
  6:30 PM

  COUNCILMEMBERS

  JED LEANO
  MAYOR

  COREY CALAYCAY  ED REECE  JENNIFER STARK  SAL MEDINA

Pursuant to the local emergency concerning the COVID-19 virus declared by
the City Council of the City of Claremont on March 19, 2020, and in
accordance  with  State  Assembly  Bill  361 (2021-2022 Regular Session,
codified at California Government Code Section 54953(e)), the following
protocols will apply to public participation for the duration of the emergency:

Members of the public will not be permitted to be physically present at meetings. To allow for public
participation, the City Council will conduct its meeting through Zoom Video Communications. To
participate in the meeting from the comfort of your own home or office, download Zoom on any phone or
computer device and copy and paste the following link into your browser to access and participate in the
live City Council meeting at 6:30 p.m.: https://zoom.us/j/256208090 or to only listen from the phone dial
(213)338-8477,  Webinar  ID:  256 208 090.  For  assistance,  please  call  (909)399-5461 or
(909)399-5463.

Members of the public who wish to address the City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or a
subject matter within the jurisdiction of the City Council may utilize the following methods. The Council
requests, but does not require, the public speakers to identify themselves.

OPTION 1: LIVE COMMENTS - Through Zoom, someone wishing to speak may virtually "raise your
hand". Wait to be called upon by the City Clerk, and then you may provide verbal comments for up to
four minutes. If you are dialing in by telephone and wish to speak, please push *9. This will “raise your
hand”.

OPTION 2: E-MAIL - Public comments may be sent via email to the City Clerk’s office at
sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us or jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. All emails will be distributed to the
City Council and imaged into the City’s document archive system.
 Page 2  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

OPTION 3: MAIL - Public comments may be mailed to Claremont City Hall, Attn: City Clerk’s Office, PO
Box 880, Claremont, CA 91711. All comments received via mail will be distributed to the City Council
and imaged into the City’s document archive system.

OPTION 4: TELEPHONICALLY - Members of the public wanting to address the City Council
telephonically are requested to inform the Claremont City Clerk's office no later than 3:00 p.m. on the
day of the meeting. The Claremont City Clerk's office can be reached at (909) 399-5461,
(909) 399-5463, sdesautels@ci.claremont.ca.us, or jcostanza@ci.claremont.ca.us. You will be called
during consideration of the item you are interested in and given up to 4 minutes to speak. The meeting
will not be live streamed through Granicus as the meeting will be live streamed through Zoom instead.

The recorded meeting will be uploaded and saved as a record.

CALL TO ORDER THE MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MOMENT OF SILENCE

ROLL CALL

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CEREMONIAL MATTERS, PRESENTATIONS, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS

Staff Introductions:

  Jacqueline Castro, Accounting Assistant
  Eric Ey, Human Services Supervisor
  Raymond Garcia, Human Services Special Events Coordinator

MAYOR AND COUNCIL

Council Item

Council Assignment Reports
City Councilmembers may serve as representatives on regional organizations. This time is
allocated for reports about their activities. For information about the Council's local,
intergovernmental  and  regional  appointments  please  visit  the  City website :
www.ci.claremont.ca.us/government/city-council/city-council-assignments-and-appointments.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

PUBLIC COMMENT
The Council has set aside this time for persons in the audience who wish to comment on items
that ARE NOT LISTED ON THIS AGENDA, but are within the jurisdiction of the City Council.
Members of the audience will later have the opportunity to address the City Council regarding ALL
OTHER ITEMS ON THE AGENDA at the time the Council considers those items.
 Page 3  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

At this time the Council will take public comment for 30 minutes. Public Comment will resume later
in the meeting if there are speakers who did not get an opportunity to speak because of the
30-minute time limit.

The Brown Act prohibits the City Council from taking action on oral requests relating to items that
are not on the agenda. The Council may engage in a brief discussion, refer the matter to staff,
and/or schedule requests for consideration at a subsequent meeting.

The Council requests, but does not require, speakers to identify themselves. When you come up
to speak, please state your name unless you wish to remain anonymous. Each speaker will be
allowed four (4) continuous minutes.

CONSENT CALENDAR
All matters listed on the consent calendar are considered to be routine. The City Council or one or
more Commissions and/or Committees have previously considered most of the items on the
consent calendar. The Council may act on these items by one motion following public comment.

Only Councilmembers may pull an item from the consent calendar for discussion.

The City Council will waive reading of resolutions and ordinances. Each resolution and ordinance
will be numbered following Council approval.

Now is the time for those in the audience to comment on the consent calendar. Each speaker will
be allowed four (4) continuous minutes to comment on items on the consent calendar.
1.  RESIGNATION OF ARCHITECTURAL COMMISSIONER PAUL SLANEY
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council accept with regret the resignation of
  Paul Slaney from the Architectural Commission.
  Attachment(s):  Resignation of Architectural Commissioner Paul Slaney

2.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING THE CITY WARRANT REGISTER
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, ALLOWING
  CERTAIN CLAIMS AND DEMANDS AND SPECIFYING THE FUNDS OUT
  OF WHICH ARE THE SAME TO BE PAID, dated February 17, 2022.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Approving City Warrant Register Dated February 17, 2022

3.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 5, 2022 AND FEBRUARY 8, 2022 (SPECIAL
  AND REGULAR)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council approve and file the special City
  Council meeting minutes of February 5, 2022, and the regular City Council
  meeting minutes of February 8, 2022.
  Attachment(s):  Draft Special Meeting Minutes of February 5, 2022
  Draft Regular Meeting Minutes of February 8, 2022
 Page 4  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

4.  RESOLUTION RECONFIRMING THE EXISTENCE OF A STATE OF EMERGENCY DUE TO
  THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council, in consideration of the ongoing state
  of emergency due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and existing public health
  orders, adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, RECONFIRMING THE EXISTENCE OF A
  STATE OF EMERGENCY DUE TO THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC.
  Attachment(s):  Resolution Reconfirming Emergency

5.  CITY OF CLAREMONT ANNUAL FINANCIAL REPORTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED JUNE 30,
  2021
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends the City Council receive and file the following letters and
  financial reports for the year ended June 30, 2021:
  A. Audit Communication and Management Letters;
  B. Auditor Letter on Internal Controls;
  C. Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR);
  D. Transportation Fund Financial Statements;
  E. Area Agency on Aging (Senior Nutrition Program) Financial Statements;
  and
  F. Auditor Letter on GANN Limit Calculation.
  Attachment(s):  Audit Communication and Management Letters
  Auditor Letter on Internal Controls
  Annual Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR)
  Transportation Fund Financial Statements
  Area Agency on Aging (Senior Nutrition Program) Financial Statements
  Auditor Letter on GANN Limit Calculation

6.  REJECT BIDS FOR RESIDENTIAL ELECTRONIC WASTE COLLECTION SERVICES AND
  UPDATE THE BULK ITEM PICKUP GUIDELINES TO ALLOW ELECTRONIC WASTE
  DISPOSAL (FUNDING SOURCE: SANITATION FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to reject all bids received
  for residential electronic waste collection services and update the City's Bulk
  Item Pickup Guidelines to allow electronic waste disposal.
 Page 5  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

7.  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO DASH CONSTRUCTION COMPANY, INC. FOR THE 2021-22
  SIDEWALK  REHABILITATION  PROJECT  TO  PROVIDE  SIDEWALK REPAIR AND
  REPLACEMENT SERVICES (FUNDING SOURCE: MEASURE R FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with DASH
  Construction Company, Inc. in the amount of $289,377, and authorize a
  project contingency of $30,623, for a total of $320,000 to provide sidewalk
  repair and replacement services between Scripps Drive and the 210
  Freeway between Towne Avenue and Mountain Avenue, Mountain Avenue
  between Base Line Road and Foothill Boulevard, and other identified
  locations throughout the City;
  B. Authorize the City Manager to enter into an agreement with RKA
  Consulting Group in the amount of $25,000 for monument preservation and
  project inspection services; and
  C. Appropriate an additional $45,000 in Measure R Funds to fully fund the
  project.
8.  ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING WILLDAN FINANCIAL SERVICES TO
  PREPARE THE 2022-23 LANDSCAPE AND LIGHTING DISTRICT ANNUAL REPORT
  (FUNDING SOURCE: LANDSCAPE AND LIGHTING DISTRICT FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY
  COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, DIRECTING
  WILLDAN FINANCIAL SERVICES, AS ENGINEER OF RECORD, TO
  PREPARE AND FILE THE 2022-23 ANNUAL REPORT PERTAINING TO
  LANDSCAPE AND LIGHTING DISTRICT NO. LL001 (PURSUANT TO THE
  LANDSCAPE AND LIGHTING ACT OF 1972).
  Attachment(s):  Proposed Resolution

PUBLIC HEARING
Pursuant to laws pertaining to redistricting, the Public Hearing for Item No. 9 will begin promptly at
8:00 p.m. Each speaker providing public comment will be allowed four (4) continuous minutes to
speak, which cannot be delegated.
9.  DISCUSSION AND SELECTION OF DRAFT REDISTRICTING  MAP(S)  FOR  FURTHER
  CONSIDERATION (FUNDING SOURCE: GENERAL FUND)
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  A. Conduct a public hearing to receive input on draft district maps, revise
  draft maps, and identify a map or maps for further consideration; and
  B. Provide direction to staff to bring the selected map or maps back to the
  City Council at the March 8, 2022 regular City Council meeting for further
  consideration and adoption into a proposed ordinance adopting revised City
  Council district voting boundaries.
 Page 6  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

  Attachment(s):  Draft Redistricting Maps
  Existing District Map
  Public Comment Received by 2/17/22

ORDINANCES - None

ADMINISTRATIVE ITEM
10. 2021-22 MID-YEAR BUDGET REPORT
  Recommendation:  Staff recommends that  the  City  Council  receive  and  file  the  2021-22
  Mid-Year Budget Report.

CONTINUED PUBLIC COMMENT
This time is reserved for those persons who were unable to speak earlier in the agenda because
of the 30-minute time restriction.

COMMISSIONS

One Police Commission Vacancy (Pending Appointment)

ADJOURNMENT

THE NEXT REGULAR MEETING OF THE CLAREMONT CITY COUNCIL WILL BE HELD ON,
MARCH 8, 2022, AT 6:30 P.M., VIA ZOOM.

A LOOK AHEAD – Upcoming Meetings and Tentative Agenda Items

New Employee Introduction
Resolution Approving Warrant Register
Approval of City Council Meeting Minutes
Resolution Declaring Continued Existence of an Emergency (COVID)
Council Priorities and Action Items
BID Annual Report
Crime-Free Multi Housing Report
Redistricting - Public Hearing #4, (Must begin at 7:00 p.m.)
Ordinance Adopting Military Equipment Use Per AB 481
Part 1 Crimes Report

MATERIALS RELATED TO AN ITEM ON THIS AGENDA, AND SUBMITTED TO THE CITY COUNCIL
AFTER PUBLICATION OF THE AGENDA, ARE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC IN THE CITY CLERK’S
OFFICE AT 207 HARVARD AVENUE, CLAREMONT, MONDAY THROUGH THURSDAY, 7 AM – 6
PM. SUBJECT MATERIALS WILL BE MADE AVAILABLE ON THE CITY WEBSITE AS SOON AS
POSSIBLE - www.ci.claremont.ca.us. For more information, please call the City Clerk’s Office at
909-399-5461.
 Page 7  City Council Agenda  February 22, 2022

IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT 0F 1990, THIS AGENDA WILL
BE MADE AVAILABLE IN APPROPRIATE ALTERNATIVE FORMATS TO PERSONS WITH
DISABILITIES. ANY PERSON WITH A DISABILITY WHO REQUIRES A MODIFICATION OR
ACCOMMODATION IN ORDER TO PARTICIPATE IN A CITY MEETING SHOULD CONTACT THE
CITY CLERK AT 909-399-5461 “VOICE” OR 1-800-735-2929 “TT/TTY” AT LEAST THREE (3)
WORKING DAYS PRIOR TO THE MEETING, IF POSSIBLE.

I, SHELLEY DESAUTELS, CITY CLERK OF THE CITY OF CLAREMONT, CALIFORNIA, HEREBY
CERTIFY UNDER PENALTY OF PERJURY THAT THE FOREGOING AGENDA WAS POSTED AT
CLAREMONT CITY HALL, 207 HARVARD AVENUE, ON FEBRUARY 17, 2022, PURSUANT TO
GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54954.2.

POST THROUGH: February 23, 2022
